title: Prove a principal-ideal dirty-fanout obstruction over K[x,y] (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration. For every field K, dirty-fanout demand `(1+xy,x²)` over K[x,y] generates the whole ring but cannot be realized with exactly one nonzero source insertion. This answers Open next question 1 of lee-phys #5139, which separates principal demand ideals from elementary-column reachability beyond finite commutative rings.

```text
demand ideal = K[x,y]
one source insertion = impossible
OPT = min(mu0+mu1, 2mu0+2c1, 2mu1+2c0)
```

The contract has exactly two arbitrary dirty output rows and one preserved disjoint source, polynomial source insertions and elementary row additions, full dirt restoration, and positive stationary coefficient-independent destination prices. The three exact Pareto-minimal count vectors are `(1,1,0,0)`, `(2,0,0,2)` and `(0,2,2,0)` in order `(P0,P1,E0,E1)`. The theorem includes characteristic two and every positive data width.

The new step reduces a hypothetical one-insertion word to the elementary orbit of Cohn's classical non-elementary matrix, then combines the obstruction with Krzysztof Wójt's #5045 source-count/return argument and restoring templates. Cohn's theorem is explicitly cited, not rechecked or presented as new. Only seven files in `research/cohn-fanout-obstruction/` are added. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

Before: #5139 proves a principal-ideal criterion over finite commutative rings and explicitly leaves nonsemilocal elementary-orbit obstructions open. After: the unit-ideal polynomial example has a complete all-word lower bound and a matching exact price envelope.

Local CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, standard library only:

- Exact integer polynomial Bezout, inverse, full affine endpoint and completion-coset identities; three attaining words and ten single-call deletion controls.
- 60,621 enumerated scalar forward/inverse pairs over F2,F3,F5,F7; 625 positive price vectors and 17 controls in total.
- All 87 field-evaluated demand pairs have explicit checked one-insertion words. These finite evaluations cannot prove the polynomial obstruction; the generated receipt records that Cohn non-elementarity is not machine-verified.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks each completed in 0.19 seconds, below their separate 120-second registered limits. Both registered checks pass, as do package metadata/provenance, committed-byte/source-history preflight, static syntax/function-size inspection and whitespace.
- Official seven-file export integrity passes. Read-only Git-free normal and optimized replays produce identical stdout; all eight exported files, including the export receipt, remain unchanged. The verifier emits a generated source-hash receipt and writes nothing.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal obstruction is the written reduction using Cohn, *On the structure of the GL2 of a ring*, IHÉS 30 (1966), §7, printed p. 26, the [example after Proposition 7.3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1966__30__5_0.pdf#page=23). Its classical non-elementarity theorem is an inherited cited dependency, not a finite certificate or a formal proof delivered here. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Extra workspace, clearing, observations, free general linear maps, and input-dependent coefficients are outside the contract. Native coefficient preparation, routing, precision/tape, stock, supplier admission and a complete multiplication theorem remain unpriced or unproved. Lean, Docker and selected scientific cold replay were not run. Every registered package command ran locally; no predecessor verifier was imported or replayed.

Scientific base is freshly fetched canonical main `ec2780e8aeb1c88acaf5e9e470ef8c68e7fbbb6c`, priority revision 7, unchanged at submission refresh. TASK.json explicitly changes the historical `bit-helper-contract` card to #5139's open algebraic side question. SOURCES.json pins predecessor proof text as provenance. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19145584) and entry/submission overlap checks cover live PRs, recent handoffs, active Discussions, account submissions, all-main README terms and distinctive merged searches. Cached entry pagination covered 315 open PRs and 4,395 Discussion records; sparse local notes and unpublished work remain coverage gaps.

Credit lee-phys #5139/#5089 for the criterion and open question, Krzysztof Wójt #5045 for the source-count classification, return lemma and repeated-insertion words, Nick Petalas #4916 for the ring-valued contract, and the Ross Richardson, Cinna Davis, Anthony, Oscar Fennell, Tekalign and retained fanout lineage. Predecessor files and credit are unchanged.

## Open next questions

Can one extra restored dirty row remove this polynomial one-insertion obstruction, and at what complete price? Start with a stabilized Cohn elementary word, retaining all three independent dirt columns and every paid row direction. A complete three-row restoring construction and matching tariff are not supplied here.

## Related open work

- #5208 proves an arbitrary-row equal-nonunit-demand tariff over commutative rings. This PR has unequal polynomial demands and excludes one insertion through a nonsemilocal elementary-column obstruction; it computes no equal-demand optimum.
- #5201 proves a signed 26-output connector optimum with three immutable sources and a mutable connector. This PR has one source and two mutable dirty output rows, with different paid gates and no shared optimum computed.
- #1865 studies commuting C3 fanout intervals in a fixed scalar word. This PR studies an unrestricted polynomial-ring gate contract and does not compute that word's native profile or ceiling.
- #3891 prices a helper-star response with a restored mutable helper. This PR has no helper row and retains a disjoint source; it supplies no H2-sem helper-star price or native supplier comparison.
- #3120 studies the selected centre's copied-information rank floor. This PR computes no native centre rank or geometry quantity.
- #3147 studies centre-source incidence, braid sparsity and sharing ceilings. Its native object and bill differ from this polynomial two-row tariff; no shared numerical quantity is compared.

The completion refresh inspected all nine other open PRs from this account created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-23T12:27:09Z. The adjacent ring-valued fanout #5208 and signed connector #5201 are listed above. The others study A4/S4/order-21/dicyclic targets, a spinor relaxation, Gaussian Schur fill and integer-transvection length. No other submission in that snapshot computes this polynomial demand tariff. No additional computations were run to check other contributions.
